info.name: API Platform Demo
info.description:
Two demo APIs on the WSO2 API Platform Gateway, both JWT-protected via jwt-auth. In both folders, jwt-auth only authenticates the caller's bearer token -- org identity for routing/rate-limiting comes from the X-Org-Name header, not any JWT claim. Folder 1: OrderManagementAPI (header-based dynamic routing + token exchange). Folder 2: AgentChatAPI (header-based, per-org AND per-org-per-use-case token-based rate limiting).

Run '1a' (Railco) and/or '1b' (Acme) to get tokens -- each saves into its OWN variable ({{railco_access_token}} / {{acme_access_token}}), so both can be held at once and every downstream request explicitly uses the right one rather than whichever token was generated most recently. NOTE: the IS instance's TLS cert is expired/self-signed -- in Postman go to Settings > General and turn OFF 'SSL certificate verification' globally, otherwise the token requests will fail with a TLS error.

exec: console.log("Saved Railco access_token to railco_access_token collection variable.");

request.description: Requests an application-level access token using Railco's own OAuth2 application (its own client_id/client_secret, and its own token endpoint via {{railco_is_base_url}} in case Railco is served by a different IS instance/tenant than Acme). Fill in railco_client_id / railco_client_secret / railco_is_base_url in the collection variables first. On success, the test script saves access_token into {{railco_access_token}} -- a separate variable from Acme's, so both tokens can be held at once and every Railco-specific request below explicitly uses this one. This token only authenticates the caller; org identity for routing comes from the X-Org-Name header set explicitly on the downstream requests, not from any claim on this token.

exec: console.log("Saved Acme access_token to acme_access_token collection variable.");

request.description: Requests an application-level access token using Acme's own OAuth2 application (its own client_id/client_secret, and its own token endpoint via {{acme_is_base_url}} in case Acme is served by a different IS instance/tenant than Railco). Fill in acme_client_id / acme_client_secret / acme_is_base_url in the collection variables first. On success, the test script saves access_token into {{acme_access_token}} -- a separate variable from Railco's, so both tokens can be held at once and every Acme-specific request below explicitly uses this one. This token only authenticates the caller; org identity for routing comes from the X-Org-Name header set explicitly on the downstream requests, not from any claim on this token.

Calls OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 using {{railco_access_token}} (run request 1a first). jwt-auth verifies the token, then dynamic-routing reads org identity from the X-Org-Name header (not the token) and routes to the matching upstreamDefinitions entry ("railco"). An X-Org-Name value with no matching upstreamDefinitions entry returns 502/503 by design (no fallback map configured); a missing X-Org-Name header returns 503 directly from dynamic-routing.

Calls OrderManagementAPI-v1.0 using {{acme_access_token}} (run request 1b first). jwt-auth verifies the token, then dynamic-routing reads org identity from the X-Org-Name header (not the token) and routes to the matching upstreamDefinitions entry ("acme"). An X-Org-Name value with no matching upstreamDefinitions entry returns 502/503 by design (no fallback map configured); a missing X-Org-Name header returns 503 directly from dynamic-routing.

item.name: 2. AgentChatAPI - Token Rate Limiting
item.description: Requests 1-3 are Railco-specific ({{railco_access_token}}, run folder 1's request 1a first); requests 4-6 are the Acme equivalents ({{acme_access_token}}, run request 1b first). Each call costs 50 tokens (mock-agent-backend.js returns a fixed X-Completion-Tokens: 50). Limits -- Railco: org=500/min, usecase1=200/min, usecase2=100/min. Acme: org=150/min, usecase1=50/min, usecase2=70/min. Requests 3 and 6 make the SAME point with OPPOSITE outcomes: after both named use-case quotas are exhausted, Railco's org budget still has room (200 left of 500) but Acme's is also fully exhausted (150 of 150 consumed) -- whether the org budget survives depends entirely on how the numbers relate to each other.

request.description: Consumes railco-usecase1-token-budget (200/min) AND railco-org-token-budget (500/min) simultaneously, since org quota has no use-case filter and matches every Railco call. At 50 tokens/call: usecase1 alone allows 4 calls before the 5th is blocked (429, x-ratelimit-quota: railco-usecase1-token-budget) -- click Send 5 times in a row to see it happen.

Consumes railco-usecase2-token-budget (100/min) AND railco-org-token-budget simultaneously. At 50 tokens/call: usecase2 alone allows 2 calls before the 3rd is blocked (429, x-ratelimit-quota: railco-usecase2-token-budget) -- click Send 3 times in a row to see it happen. After running this AND request 1 above to full exhaustion, the org budget has consumed 200 (usecase1) + 100 (usecase2) = 300 of its 500 total -- 200 still remaining, proven by request 3 below.

item.name: 3. Railco org quota STILL has room (different use-case, after 1+2 exhausted)

exec: pm.test("Org quota still had room -- 200 even though usecase1/usecase2 are individually exhausted", function () {

request.description: THE DEMO POINT: X-Use-Case-Id here is "usecase-onboarding" -- a use-case with NO dedicated quota configured, so only railco-org-token-budget (500/min) applies to this call, not any per-use-case limit. Run this AFTER exhausting requests 1 and 2 above (usecase1 and usecase2 both individually blocked at 429). This call still succeeds with 200, proving the org-wide budget still has room (500 - 200 - 100 = 200 remaining) even though both specific use-case quotas are maxed out -- org and use-case budgets are independent, and a 3rd/other use-case is only ever gated by the org-wide ceiling.

Consumes acme-usecase1-token-budget (50/min) AND acme-org-token-budget (150/min) simultaneously. At 50 tokens/call, acme-usecase1's limit (50) is consumed in a single call -- the 1st call succeeds (pre-check 0<50), the 2nd is blocked immediately (pre-check 50 not<50, 429, x-ratelimit-quota: acme-usecase1-token-budget) -- click Send twice to see it happen.

Consumes acme-usecase2-token-budget (70/min) AND acme-org-token-budget simultaneously. At 50 tokens/call: call 1 pre-checks 0<70 (allowed, running total becomes 50), call 2 pre-checks 50<70 (still allowed even though the next deduction overshoots the nominal 70 limit -- running total becomes 100), call 3 pre-checks 100<70 -- false, blocked (429, x-ratelimit-quota: acme-usecase2-token-budget). Click Send 3 times to see it happen. After running this AND request 4 above to full exhaustion, the org budget has consumed 50 (usecase1) + 100 (usecase2) = 150 of its 150 total -- fully exhausted, unlike Railco's org budget which still had room. See request 6 below.

item.name: 6. Acme org quota ALSO exhausted (different use-case, after 4+5 exhausted -- unlike Railco)

exec: pm.test("Org quota is also exhausted -- 429, unlike Railco where it still had room", function () {

request.description: THE CONTRASTING DEMO POINT: unlike request 3 (Railco), this one is expected to return 429, not 200. Acme's usecase1 (50) + usecase2 (70, but only 100 actually consumed before blocking) budgets happen to sum to exactly Acme's org budget (150) -- 50 + 100 = 150. So once both named use-case quotas are individually exhausted, acme-org-token-budget is ALSO fully consumed, and this different/unnamed use-case gets blocked too (429, x-ratelimit-quota: acme-org-token-budget). Run this AFTER exhausting requests 4 and 5 above. This is a deliberate contrast with Railco (request 3): whether the org budget still has headroom after every named use-case is exhausted depends entirely on how the numbers are configured relative to each other -- it is not guaranteed, and Acme's current limits happen to leave zero room.
